---
title: "Tokenizer"
subtitle: "Domain BPE vocabulary for poker hand histories"
---

# Why a custom tokenizer?

Poker states are dense with symbols (`BB`, `P1`, suit ranks, stack sizes). A
general English BPE wastes capacity on irrelevant merges. Training a
Byte-Level BPE on the hand corpus yields a compact vocabulary tuned to this
domain.

# Training

```bash
python scripts/train_tokenizer.py
# or: pokerai-tokenizer
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-tok-settings
#| tbl-cap: "Tokenizer settings from `pokerai.config` / `pokerai.data.tokenizer`."

from pokerai import config
import pandas as pd

pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {"Setting": "Algorithm", "Value": "Byte-Level BPE"},
        {"Setting": "Target vocab size", "Value": config.VOCAB_SIZE},
        {"Setting": "Min frequency", "Value": 2},
        {"Setting": "BOS", "Value": config.BOS_TOKEN},
        {"Setting": "EOS", "Value": config.EOS_TOKEN},
        {"Setting": "PAD", "Value": config.PAD_TOKEN},
        {"Setting": "model_max_length", "Value": config.N_POSITIONS},
        {"Setting": "Input file", "Value": str(config.HANDS_RAW.relative_to(config.REPO_ROOT))},
        {"Setting": "Output dir", "Value": str(config.TOKENIZER_DIR.relative_to(config.REPO_ROOT))},
    ]
)
```

# Special tokens

::: {.callout-important}
## BOS and EOS must be distinct

`<|startoftext|>` and `<|endoftext|>` are separate tokens. If BOS and EOS share
an ID, the model cannot tell “hand starting” from “hand ending,” which corrupts
sequence-boundary learning. After renaming specials, **retrain the tokenizer and
rerun every downstream step**—token IDs shift.
:::

# Diagnostics printed at train time

The tokenizer script reports:

- sample hand + token count
- max / average tokens per hand across the corpus

Use the max length to confirm `N_POSITIONS` (default **384**) is adequate. Long
sequences are truncated from the **front** during encoding so the action tokens
at the end are preserved.
